title: Mac call-audio capture (system audio, macOS 14.2+)
story: On my Mac I chose call audio and Grillo heard the other people on the call. When I had turned off the audio-recording permission, Grillo told me within a couple of seconds where to turn it back on, instead of quietly recording silence. On my old Mac it simply said I need a newer macOS. Before this story call audio on any Mac was refused as unsupported.

checks.criterion: On macOS 14.2+, call audio is captured through Electron's loopback
checks.steps: On a Mac with macOS 14.2 or later, grant Grillo in Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart Grillo. Start a call-audio capture, play a made-up test tone for 15 s, then stop.
checks.expected: About three call slices of 80 000 samples, numbered 0 to 2, that carry the tone.

checks.criterion: A missing permission is reported as permission missing, with where to grant it
checks.steps: On a 14.2+ Mac, turn Grillo off in Screen & System Audio Recording, restart Grillo, then start a call-audio capture.
checks.expected: Within about 2 s, a refusal naming System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, and no slices.

checks.criterion: A Mac older than 14.2 gets a typed unsupported answer
checks.steps: On macOS 14.1 or earlier, start a call-audio capture.
checks.expected: A message that macOS 14.2 or later is needed, and no screen-sharing prompt.
